key_insight: Current vision-language models are not yet reliable enough for fully objective medical image quality assessment, especially when images are corrupted or metadata is present.
clinical_relevance: In clinical workflows, unstable quality scoring could affect decisions about whether an image is usable, so reliability, privacy, and bias need attention before deployment.
method: Zero-shot benchmark of 16 VLMs on the MediMeta-C dataset
Tested seven corruption types across five severity levels
Compared seven medical imaging modalities and varied textual metadata such as demographics, expertise, infrastructure, and institution
evidence_signal: Pixelation caused the largest average score drop (-20.58%), while brightness had minimal impact (-0.81%); institutional prestige raised scores by +17.15% and equipment age lowered them by -14.7%.
watch_item: Because privacy-preserving pixelation and contextual metadata can strongly change scores, using VLMs for MIQA without safeguards may introduce reliability, privacy, and bias risks.
paper_title: Assessing VLM Reliability for Medical Image Quality Evaluation Under Corruption and Bias
